newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia metals sector sees tough March qtr.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia metals sector sees tough March qtr.

text.p: Metals, manufacturing and engineering firms expect business conditions to remain difficult, reinforcing the need for further interest rate cuts, an industry survey said on Wednesday.

The Metal Trades Industry Association December quarter survey of business conditions said import competition was high, the high value of the Australian dollar and low demand in Asian markets was hitting exports.
One-third of firms surveyed expected to continue cutting employment levels in the March quarter.

"Subdued market conditions are mitigating against a continuation of the very strong plant and equipment investment levels of recent months," association chief executive Bob Herbert said in a statement.
"All up, these conditions certainly justify interest rate relief.
"The economy can grow faster without increasing inflation."

Herbert said falling inflation and a rising exchange rate meant only a small part of the 1.5 percentage point reduction in official interest rates since July had flowed through to business in real rate reductions.
The survey of 250 companies in January reported a seasonal pick-up in the December quarter, but a subdued outlook for most of calendar 1997.

"In terms of the general business outlook, prospects are unchanged on those reported three months earlier, with only a gradual improvement in activity forecast through to September 1997 and no early return to the levels prevailing in 1994 and 1995," the survey said.

The survey found more than one-third of businesses expected to cut jobs further in the March quarter, most firms expected demand and production to pick up, de-stocking to continue and investment to weaken.

The number of respondents which expected to increase investment over the next 12 months fell to 49.8 percent from 50.5 percent in the last survey, while 19.4 percent expected to decrease capital spending, compared with 14 percent in the September quarter survey.
